lem-chebyshev-rkc-bounds-and-endpoint-de:
## Statement

Let $T_n$ and $U_n$ be the real evaluation functions of the Chebyshev polynomials defined by [[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]]. For every natural $n$,

$$|T_n(x)|\le 1,\qquad |U_n(x)|\le n+1\quad(-1\le x\le1),$$

and for $n\ge1$, $|T_n(x)|>1$ whenever $|x|>1$. Also,

$$T_n(1)=1,\quad T_n(-1)=(-1)^n,\quad U_n(1)=n+1,\quad U_n(-1)=(-1)^n(n+1).$$

For every natural $n\ge1$, $T_n$ has degree $n$ and leading coefficient $2^{n-1}$, while $U_n$ has degree $n$ and leading coefficient $2^n$. This degree and leading-coefficient assertion is exactly the content of [[lem-chebyshev-degree-leading-coefficients-and-extreme-values]]; that item does not assert an extremum bound.

The evaluation functions are twice differentiable at $1$, with

$$T_n'(1)=n^2,\qquad T_n''(1)=\frac{n^2(n^2-1)}{3}.$$

Here each natural number in a real formula denotes its canonical real image ([[def-canonical-natural]]), and powers use [[def-integer-power]].
def-explicit-runge-kutta-tableau-and-sta:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be an open time-state domain, and let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be the right-hand side of a first-order initial-value problem in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. An explicit $s$-stage Runge–Kutta tableau consists of a positive integer $s$, real coefficients $a_{ij}$, $b_i$, and $c_i$ with $a_{ij}=0$ whenever $j\ge i$, and
$$c_i=\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}\qquad(1\le i\le s).$$
The finite row sum is empty, hence $c_1=0$.

For a step size $h>0$ from an admitted base pair $(t,y)\in D$, compute in order
$$Y_i=y+h\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}K_j,\qquad t_i=t+c_i h,\qquad K_i=f(t_i,Y_i)\quad(i=1,\ldots,s).$$
The strict lower-triangular condition makes each stage depend only on already computed slopes; no implicit stage equation is solved. If every stage is defined, the candidate output is
$$y^+=y+h\sum_{i=1}^s b_iK_i.$$

The procedure accepts an exact right-hand-side evaluation oracle that returns either the value $f(t_i,Y_i)$ or an evaluation-failure status. Before each query it checks $(t_i,Y_i)\in D$. It returns domain-failure with the first failing stage if that check fails, evaluation-failure with the stage index if the oracle fails, and domain-failure at output if $(t+h,y^+)\notin D$. Otherwise it returns success with $(t+h,y^+)$. In the exact mathematical model the oracle returns $f$ at every point of $D$; the failure branch records only an unavailable numerical evaluation. On success this is a one-step map in the sense of [[def-one-step-ode-method-local-defect-order-and-stability]].
alg-rkc1-chebyshev:
## Definition

This algorithm takes an autonomous vector field $f$ on an open state domain $V\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, an admitted initial state $y$, a step $h>0$, and an integer stage count $s\ge1$. Define stage abscissae $c_j=j^2/s^2$ for $0\le j\le s$. Set $Y_0=y$. Before each query check that its stage state belongs to $V$; if it does not, return domain-failure with that stage index. If the right-hand-side evaluator fails, return evaluation-failure with that stage index. Query at $Y_0$ and, on success, set $Y_1=Y_0+(h/s^2)f(Y_0)$. For $j=2,\ldots,s$, query at $Y_{j-1}$ and, on success, set
$$Y_j=2Y_{j-1}-Y_{j-2}+\frac{2h}{s^2}f(Y_{j-1}).$$
If the final state $Y_s$ is outside $V$, return output-domain-failure; otherwise return success with $Y_s$ at time $t+h$.

For a nonautonomous equation $y'=f(t,y)$, apply the same algorithm to the autonomous augmented field $\widetilde f(t,y)=(1,f(t,y))$. Its time component follows the same recurrence and equals $t+c_jh$ at stage $j$, with $c_s=1$. This is the first-order undamped RKC method; its scalar linear stability polynomial is established separately.

The stability analysis uses $T_s$ and $U_s$ from [[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]]; this item defines the executable recurrence and does not itself assert an order or stability theorem.
alg-rkc2-linear-chebyshev:
## Definition

Input a finite-dimensional real vector space $V$, a linear endomorphism $A:V\to V$, an initial vector $y\in V$, a step $h>0$, and an integer stage count $s\ge2$. If a numerical application of $A$ reports failure, return that failure with its stage index. Define
$$w_1=\frac{3}{s^2-1},\qquad b_s=\frac{s^2-1}{3s^2},\qquad a_s=1-b_s.$$
Set $V_0=y$ and $V_1=V_0+w_1hA(V_0)$. For $j=2,\ldots,s$, compute
$$V_j=2V_{j-1}+2w_1hA(V_{j-1})-V_{j-2}.$$
Return $a_sV_0+b_sV_s$. Each stage uses one application of $A$; no implicit system is solved. The output is the one-step update for the autonomous linear equation $y'=Ay$. Here $T_s$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial defined by [[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]]; the equivalent polynomial in $hA$ and its certified real stability interval are proved separately.
alg-rkc2-nonlinear:
## Definition

Input a first-order right-hand side $f(t,y)$ on an open time-state domain, an admitted pair $(t,y)$, a step $h>0$, and an integer stage count $s\ge2$. Set
$$w_1=\frac{3}{s^2-1},\qquad b_0=b_1=b_2=\frac14,\qquad b_j=\frac{j^2-1}{3j^2}\ (3\le j\le s),\qquad a_j=1-b_j\ (0\le j\le s).$$
For the stages define $c_0=0$, $c_1=b_1w_1$, and $c_j=b_jw_1j^2$ for $2\le j\le s$. Put $Y_0=y$. Before each query check that its time-state input belongs to the declared domain; if not, return domain-failure with that stage index. If the right-hand-side evaluator reports failure, return evaluation-failure with that stage index. Query $k_0=f(t,Y_0)$ and on success set $Y_1=Y_0+b_1w_1h k_0$. For each $j=2,\ldots,s$, define
$$\mu_j=\frac{2b_j}{b_{j-1}},\qquad \nu_j=-\frac{b_j}{b_{j-2}},\qquad m_j=\frac{2b_jw_1}{b_{j-1}},\qquad g_j=-a_{j-1}m_j,$$
query $k_{j-1}=f(t+c_{j-1}h,Y_{j-1})$, and on success set
$$Y_j=(1-\mu_j-\nu_j)y+\mu_jY_{j-1}+\nu_jY_{j-2}+m_jh k_{j-1}+g_jh k_0.$$
If $(t+h,Y_s)$ is outside the declared domain, return output-domain-failure; otherwise return success with $(t+h,Y_s)$. All stages use only the initial state and already computed values, so the procedure contains no implicit solve.

For an autonomous field, omit the time argument. The abscissae above are the exact time coordinates obtained by applying the recurrence to the augmented equation $t'=1$; in particular $c_s=1$. Order, stability, and stage-amplification claims are separate proved items.

The coefficient $b_2$ agrees with the displayed formula at $j=2$; it is listed among the base values to make the recurrence unambiguous. The Chebyshev identities used to derive these coefficients are supplied by [[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]].
def-euler-midpoint-rk4-tableaus:
## Definition

The following are the explicit Runge–Kutta tableaus in the convention of [[def-explicit-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-map]].

Forward Euler has $s=1$, $A=(0)$, $b=(1)$, and $c=(0)$.

Explicit midpoint has $s=2$, $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\[2pt]1/2&0\end{pmatrix}$, $b=(0,1)$, and $c=(0,1/2)$.

The classical four-stage Runge–Kutta method has $s=4$, $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0&0\\[2pt]1/2&0&0&0\\[2pt]0&1/2&0&0\\[2pt]0&0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $b=(1/6,1/3,1/3,1/6)$, and $c=(0,1/2,1/2,1)$.

Each displayed $c_i$ is the row sum required in the definition of an explicit tableau. These tableaus specify the stage equations; their order and scalar stability functions are proved separately.
alg-ssprk33:
## Definition

Input an initial pair $(t,y)$, a step $h>0$, an open time-state domain $D$, and a right-hand-side evaluator for $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$. Before each query, check that its time-state pair is in $D$; return domain-failure with that stage index if it is not. If the evaluator reports failure, return evaluation-failure with that stage index. Execute:

1. Query $f(t,y)$. On success set $Y_1=y+h f(t,y)$.
2. Query $f(t+h,Y_1)$. On success set $Y_2=\frac34y+\frac14\bigl(Y_1+h f(t+h,Y_1)\bigr)$.
3. Query $f(t+h/2,Y_2)$. On success set $y^+=\frac13y+\frac23\bigl(Y_2+h f(t+h/2,Y_2)\bigr)$.
4. If $(t+h,y^+)\notin D$, return output-domain-failure; otherwise return success with $(t+h,y^+)$.

The equivalent tableau has $c=(0,1,1/2)$, $b=(1/6,1/6,2/3)$, and rows of $A$ equal to $(0,0,0)$, $(1,0,0)$, and $(1/4,1/4,0)$. The procedure uses only explicit function evaluations; it has no implicit stage solve. If a numerical evaluator can fail even at a domain point, its failure is returned unchanged with the corresponding stage index. The exact mathematical method assumes all queried values exist.
prop-euler-midpoint-rk4-orders-and-stabi:
## Statement

Under the smoothness and compact-tube hypotheses of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]], the forward Euler, explicit midpoint, and classical four-stage tableaus of [[def-euler-midpoint-rk4-tableaus]] have uniform local orders at least one, two, and four, respectively.

For the scalar test equation $y'=\lambda y$, set $z=h\lambda$. The corresponding stability functions, defined by $y^+=R(z)y$, are
$$R_{\mathrm E}(z)=1+z,\qquad R_{\mathrm M}(z)=1+z+\frac{z^2}{2},\qquad R_{\mathrm{RK4}}(z)=1+z+\frac{z^2}{2}+\frac{z^3}{6}+\frac{z^4}{24}.$$
The absolute stability region of a listed method is $\{z\in\mathbb C:|R(z)|\le1\}$. On the negative real axis, the Euler and midpoint regions are exactly $[-2,0]$. No maximal real interval is asserted here for RK4.
prop-rkc-stability-intervals-and-stage-d:
## Statement

On the scalar test equation $y'=\lambda y$, write $z=h\lambda$ and let $R(z)$ be the factor by which a successful method step multiplies $y$.

For first-order RKC with $s\ge1$ stages,
$$R_{1,s}(z)=T_s(1+z/s^2).$$
It has degree $s$, satisfies $R_{1,s}(0)=R'_{1,s}(0)=1$, and its real absolute stability set $\{z\in\mathbb R:|R_{1,s}(z)|\le1\}$ is exactly $[-2s^2,0]$.

For second-order RKC with $s\ge2$ stages, both the linear algorithm and the scalar-linear specialization of the nonlinear algorithm have
$$R_{2,s}(z)=a_s+b_sT_s(1+w_1z),\qquad w_1=\frac{3}{s^2-1},\quad b_s=\frac{s^2-1}{3s^2},\quad a_s=1-b_s.$$
This polynomial has degree $s$ and satisfies $R_{2,s}(0)=R'_{2,s}(0)=R''_{2,s}(0)=1$. It is absolutely stable on the real interval $[-2(s^2-1)/3,0]$; this is a certified interval and is not claimed to be the maximal real stability set.

Let $A$ be a self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathbb R^d$ with its Euclidean inner product and assume $\langle Av,v\rangle\le0$ for every $v$. Let $\rho=\max_i(-\lambda_i)$, where $\lambda_i$ are the eigenvalues of $A$. If $h\rho\le2s^2$, first-order RKC is nonexpansive in the Euclidean norm; if $h\rho\le2(s^2-1)/3$, linear second-order RKC is nonexpansive. The same linear contraction statement holds for the nonlinear RKC method when applied to $f(y)=Ay$. No corresponding claim is made for nonnormal matrices.
lem-rkc-chebyshev-stage-perturbation-amp:
## Statement

Let $A$ be a self-adjoint endomorphism of $\mathbb R^d$ with its Euclidean inner product and $\langle Av,v\rangle\le0$. For first-order RKC assume the integer stage count $s\ge1$ and $h\rho\le2s^2$; for linear second-order RKC assume $s\ge2$ and $h\rho\le2(s^2-1)/3$, where $\rho=\max_i(-\lambda_i(A))$. In either branch, let $X=I+hA/s^2$ or $X=I+w_1hA$, respectively.

Write $Y_j$ for the generic recurrence stage; in the second-order branch this is the $V_j$ of [[alg-rkc2-linear-chebyshev]]. Model the error injected into each recurrence update by vectors $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_s$:
$$\widehat Y_0=y,\qquad \widehat Y_1=X\widehat Y_0+\delta_1,\qquad \widehat Y_j=2X\widehat Y_{j-1}-\widehat Y_{j-2}+\delta_j\quad(2\le j\le s).$$
If $\|\delta_j\|_2\le\varepsilon$ for every $j$, then the final stage error relative to the unperturbed recurrence is at most
$$\|\widehat Y_s-Y_s\|_2\le\frac{s(s+1)}2\,\varepsilon.$$
For linear second-order RKC the returned state multiplies this bound by $b_s\le1$. An additional output perturbation of norm $\varepsilon_{\rm out}$ adds at most $\varepsilon_{\rm out}$. This is a bound for the stated additive-error model; it does not assert a floating-point error size.
prop-ssprk33-third-order-and-convex-pres:
## Statement

Assume the smoothness and compact-tube hypotheses of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]]. The step in [[alg-ssprk33]] has uniform local order at least three.

For an autonomous field, take an initial state $y\in C$, where $C$ is a convex subset of the state domain, and let $E_h(u)=u+h f(u)$ be the forward-Euler map. If $E_h(C)\subseteq C$ and all displayed stages are admitted, then every SSPRK(3,3) stage and the output lie in $C$. If $\Phi:C\to\mathbb R$ is convex, meaning $\Phi(\theta u+(1-\theta)v)\le\theta\Phi(u)+(1-\theta)\Phi(v)$ for $u,v\in C$ and $0\le\theta\le1$, and $\Phi(E_h(u))\le\Phi(u)$ for every $u\in C$, then $\Phi$ does not increase at any of the three stages or at the output.

For a nonautonomous field, assume the initial state $y\in C$ and that the forward-Euler maps at the actual stage start times $t$, $t+h$, and $t+h/2$ preserve $C$ and satisfy the stated $\Phi$ inequality on all admitted stage states. These conditions are premises of the theorem; the method alone does not assert positivity, total-variation diminishing, or any universal invariant-region property.
thm-nonlinear-rkc2-order-two-and-global-:
## Statement

Fix $s\ge2$ and $T>0$. Let $f(t,y)$ be $C^2$ on an open time-state domain, and let the exact IVP solution $y$ be defined on $[0,T]$. Assume its derivatives through order three and the derivatives of $f$ through order two are bounded on a compact convex tube $K$ contained in the domain. Assume the stage recursion of [[alg-rkc2-nonlinear]] is admitted from every starting state in $K$ for sufficiently small uniform steps and that every stage and output remains in $K$. Assume all line segments used in Taylor expansions stay in $K$, and that on each state slice of $K$, $f$ is Lipschitz in its state argument with one common constant $L_f$. Evaluation failures and domain failures are absent. The global-error claim additionally assumes the exact and numerical trajectories stay in $K$.

Then the nonlinear RKC2 method has a uniform one-step defect bound $C_s h^3$ and one-step stability bound $(1+L_s h)$ on that tube, for constants $C_s,L_s$ independent of the step index and $h$ (but allowed to depend on fixed $s$ and the tube bounds).

For $h=T/N$, start the method at $y(0)$ and suppose its numerical stages and states remain in the same tube for all $N$ steps. Then the global grid error is at most
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le \begin{cases}C_s\frac{\exp(L_sT)-1}{L_s}h^2,&L_s>0,\\ C_sTh^2,&L_s=0.\end{cases}$$
The statement is fixed-stage and fixed-time. It gives no uniform-in-$s$ accuracy, nonlinear stability, positivity, or stiffness-uniform accuracy.
